analysis.title: Iran War Chartpack Week 36: Calm Before The Storm?
key_insights: SEB sees the post-midterm period as a risk window for renewed US/Israeli fighting with Iran. Reports say Netanyahu pressed Trump to strike right after the midterms, while Trump wanted talks to continue.

The prevailing Middle East equilibrium is described as unstable absent a diplomatic breakthrough. Iran is willing to withstand the blockade for months, and some analysts say the US Navy may have less than six months to hold an effective blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
Trump's options are to continue the blockade, accept Iranian demands and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, or intensify the war. SEB says acquiescence is unlikely given US domestic political costs.

SEB's three short-term scenarios are a deal (cold peace), talks fizzle (no war, no peace), and limited war with a nuclear focus. A larger-scale war is a fourth path, with an all-out infrastructure war and hard Iranian retaliation across the region.
Scenario-weighted Brent in 3 months implies $98.9/b against a latest market price of $99.0/b. SEB assigns 0.35 to negotiations and 0.6 to prolonged conflict across its six scenarios.

Renewed conflict (scenario 6) carries 0.35 probability and a $100-150/b Brent range with large sustained disruption of energy and shipping. The US-and-Israel-overwhelm-Iran case carries 0.05 and a $50-60/b range.

EIA's latest STEO expects Brent spot to average $105/b in 4Q26, $14/b above last month's STEO, and $84/b in 2027. Middle East flows stay constrained through 4Q26 and most regional production returns to pre-conflict averages by end of 2Q27.

Regional crude production shut-ins averaged 4.8m b/d in September, down from 5.8m b/d in August and 10.9m b/d at the May peak. Global inventories fell 1.9m b/d in 3Q26 and are expected to fall another 0.7m b/d in 4Q26.

The gasoil-Brent crack spread rose from about $27/bbl at the start of 2025 to a peak of $101/bbl in September. Drivers are Iran war disruption of product flows, Ukrainian strikes on Russian diesel exports, European refining limits and seasonal demand.
Long-dated DFL (a physical-versus-paper crude price spread) divergence stays sticky, which SEB reads as the market pricing supply pressure into 2027.

Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure escalated in October, with 15-20 distinct attack waves on six of seven days and strikes on King Khalid International Airport and an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran. Saudi Arabia struck Houthi fuel storage on Oct 13.

Houthi attacks and a declared blockade on Saudi-linked vessels have reduced traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and put upward pressure on oil prices. Bab al-Mandeb is a second chokepoint that exposes the Hormuz workaround.

The US is leaning on economic measures, including possible targeting of financial networks that help Iran sell oil, such as Chinese banks, yuan payments and Hong Kong institutions. Munitions depletion and reduced base presence limit military options.

CSIS estimates US stocks of Tomahawk, THAAD and Patriot missiles will take 3+ years to return to prewar levels, with Tomahawk back in late 2030 to early 2031. SEB flags a window of vulnerability for an Indo-Pacific conflict.
Iran's storage is limited. Estimates put remaining crude storage at 20-35mb, or roughly 2-3 weeks before production cuts, and losing about 1.6m b/d would strain Iran's external balance.
Iran's headline inflation reached 88% in July and food inflation 128%. Iran is in its eighth currency crisis since 2016.
Prediction markets show low expectations of a Strait of Hormuz reopening. The 60 transit-call threshold is only about two-thirds of the 2025 average number of transit calls per IMF PortWatch.

SEB's weekly trade-route table (Expeditors, as of Oct 28) shows air and customs restricted in Abu Dhabi, Bahrain, Dubai, Kuwait, Qatar and Saudi Arabia, with ocean freight restricted in all of those except Dubai-adjacent notes where it is also restricted, and ground freight and warehousing operational throughout.

sector_views.rationale: SEB does not state a sector stance. The report points to elevated Brent, soaring diesel cracks and sticky long-dated physical premiums, with EIA seeing supply constraints into 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The probability-weighted scenario price is in line with futures, so SEB's scenario mix does not point to mispricing.
EIA raised its 4Q26 forecast by $14/b from last month's STEO.
EIA expects prices to fall as regional production returns to pre-conflict averages by end of 2Q27.
Shut-ins fell from 5.8m b/d in August and 10.9m b/d at the May peak, but flows stay constrained through 4Q26.
EIA expects a further 0.7m b/d draw on average in 4Q26.
Up from about $27/bbl at the start of 2025, pointing to severe product tightness in Europe.
Record-high inflation alongside a falling currency adds economic pressure on the regime.

risk_factors: Renewed US/Israeli strikes after the midterms and Iranian retaliation or pre-emption.
Wider regional war with attacks on energy, water and undersea cables.
Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and a second chokepoint at Bab al-Mandeb.
Gulf oil facilities remain vulnerable to attacks from Iraqi militias and the Houthis.
Depleted US munitions and reduced base presence limit military options.
Sovereign credit risk is rising again.
Iranian attacks on tankers may intensify ahead of the midterms.
charts_described: Scenario table: Brent in 3 months, SEB scenario-weighted implied $98.9/b vs latest market price $99.0/b.
CSIS munitions table: Tomahawk 1,000+ used with return to prewar inventory late 2030 to early 2031, Patriot 1,060-1,430 used with return mid-2029.
vol_and_positioning: SEB notes oil volatility remains elevated, but the text gives no specific implied volatility levels.
CDS spreads for sovereigns are rising again, according to the credit risk section headline.
geopolitical: Concern over renewed US/Israeli strikes on Iran after the US midterms, with Netanyahu reportedly pressing Trump to strike immediately afterward.
US naval blockade of Iran and Iranian attacks on tankers in the Gulf, with the Strait of Hormuz still disrupted.
Qatar says it is working towards an interim deal, while Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi says Iran's conditions have not changed.
Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports and energy sites, and Saudi strikes on Houthi fuel infrastructure.
Houthis reportedly encircled Taiz City as of Oct 12 and may threaten Aden.
Iranian leadership is described as shifting toward offensive deterrence, with Arab intelligence officials citing planning to widen the war.
Mojtaba Khamenei has been Supreme Leader since March 2026 and has not been seen in public.
US plans for new economic pressure on Iran's oil financing networks, potentially including Chinese banks and Hong Kong.

tension_points.bull_case: Qatar says it is working towards an interim deal, Trump said "No" when asked about striking Iran after the elections, and Vance said no deadline has been set. SEB calls a skinny deal the base case in its June note.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran's conditions have not moved, Netanyahu is pressing for strikes after the midterms, and SEB assigns 0.6 probability to prolonged conflict across its scenarios.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A strike campaign after the US midterms, or Iran dropping its conditions, including lifting the port blockade and unfreezing assets, would settle which way it goes.

theme_stances.key_argument: Absent diplomatic progress, the road to intensified conflict remains open and may be inversely correlated with the pressure on the Iranian regime.
theme_stances.evidence: the prevailing geopolitical equilibrium in the Middle East is inherently unstable

theme_stances.theme: Strait of Hormuz oil supply disruption
theme_stances.key_argument: Elevated crude oil prices and disruptions in downstream products point to concerns over shipping security, escalation risks and stockpiles.
theme_stances.evidence: Sticky longer-dated DFL divergence indicate market is pricing in supply pressure into 2027
